title: Cessna Citation CJ4

sources.title: New aircraft in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024
Cessna Citation CJ4 pilot information (public knowledge)
JoyPro function tables MSFS2020/2024 and X-Plane 11/12 (DB/Functions)

intro: The Cessna Citation CJ4 is a small business jet with two engines. It is certified to be flown by a single pilot. The flight data are shown on four large Collins Pro Line 21 screens. Two throttle levers sit on a short pedestal; there is no autothrottle and no thrust reverser on the standard aircraft.

areas.name: Glareshield
areas.text: The strip below the windscreen with the warning lights, the display panels and the autopilot panel.

panels.name: Glareshield: autopilot and display controls
panels.text: The strip under the windscreen. It has the warning lights, the panels to set the screens and the autopilot panel.
panels.context: The pilot uses it to set the screens and to tell the autopilot what to do.

controls.name: MASTER WARNING / CAUTION lights
controls.text: These lights get the pilot's attention when something is wrong. The red one is a warning, the amber one a caution. Pressing a light resets it.
controls.context: The engine and alert screen then says what is wrong.

controls.name: Display control panels
controls.text: These panels set what the screens show: the page format, how far the map reaches and the air-pressure setting for the altimeter.
controls.context: Each side of the cockpit has its own.

controls.name: AP / YD buttons
controls.text: AP switches the autopilot on or off. YD switches the yaw damper, a helper that steadies the tail, on or off.
controls.context: With the autopilot on, the plane flies by itself while the pilot watches.

controls.name: HDG / NAV / APPR / B/C buttons
controls.text: These buttons choose how the autopilot steers: HDG holds a compass direction, NAV follows a route or radio beam, APPR flies an approach, B/C uses the back side of a runway beam.
controls.context: The pilot picks the mode that fits the phase of flight.

controls.name: FLC / VS / ALT / VNAV buttons
controls.text: These buttons choose how the autopilot climbs or descends: FLC changes the level at a held speed, VS holds a climb rate, ALT holds the height and VNAV follows the planned climb and descent.
controls.context: The pilot picks the one that fits the instruction from air traffic control.

controls.name: HDG, CRS, ALT knobs and VS wheel
controls.text: These dials set the targets: the HDG knob sets the compass direction, the CRS knob the course of a radio beam, the ALT knob the height and the VS wheel the climb or sink rate.
controls.context: The numbers appear on the pilot's flying screen.

areas.name: Four large displays
areas.text: The four big screens in the middle of the panel and the landing gear handle.

panels.name: Four large displays
panels.text: Four big flat screens made by Collins (Pro Line 21) show the flight data, the map, the engines and checklists.
panels.context: They replace the many round dials of older planes.

controls.name: PFD (primary flight display, each pilot)
controls.text: This screen shows how the plane flies: tilt, speed, height and the autopilot modes.
controls.context: It is the pilot's main flying screen.

controls.name: MFD (multi-function displays, two in the centre)
controls.text: These two screens in the middle show the map, the engine data and checklists.
controls.context: The pilot picks the page with the display control panel.

controls.name: Standby instrument
controls.text: A small separate instrument which shows tilt, speed and height. It works even if the big screens fail.
controls.context: It is the backup if the main displays are lost.

controls.name: Landing gear handle

positions.name: DOWN
positions.text: The landing gear is lowered and locked.

controls.text: This handle lifts the wheels after take-off and lowers them before landing.
controls.context: The wheels fold away in flight to reduce drag.

areas.name: Lower switch panels
areas.text: The switch panels below the displays.

panels.name: Lower switch panels
panels.text: Panels below the screens with the switches for the electricity, the engine start, the lights, the anti-ice and the parking brake.
panels.context: The pilot uses them while preparing the plane and in bad weather.

controls.name: Battery and generator switches
controls.text: These switches connect the battery and the engine generators to the plane's electric system.
controls.context: They are switched on early when preparing the plane.

controls.name: Engine start / ignition
controls.text: These buttons start the engines and control the ignition, which makes the sparks to light the fuel.
controls.context: The pilot uses them after the electricity is on.

controls.name: Exterior lights
controls.text: These switches turn on the outside lights.
controls.context: The pilot uses them to be seen and to see the runway.

controls.name: Anti-ice switches (engine, wing, windshield)
controls.text: These switches turn on the heating that keeps ice off the engine inlets, the wings and the windscreen.
controls.context: The pilot uses them when flying in icing conditions.

controls.name: Parking brake T-handle
controls.text: This T-shaped handle sets the parking brake, which holds the wheels still while parked. It is pulled with the toe brakes pressed.
controls.context: It sits at the lower left of the pilot's panel.

areas.name: Pedestal
areas.text: The short pedestal between the pilots with the throttles, flap and speed brake levers and the keypads.

panels.name: Pedestal
panels.text: A short pedestal between the pilots with the two throttle levers, the speed brake and flap levers, the trim controls and the flight computer keypads.
panels.context: The pilot uses it on every flight.

controls.name: Throttles (CUTOFF, IDLE, CRU, CLB, TO)

positions.name: CUTOFF
positions.text: The fuel is off and the engine is stopped.

positions.name: IDLE
positions.text: The engine runs at its lowest power.

controls.text: Two levers set the power of the two engines. They have notches (detents) that the engine computer (FADEC) uses to set power for cruise, climb or take-off.
controls.context: The plane has no autothrottle, so the pilot moves the levers by hand.

controls.name: Speed brake lever
controls.text: This lever lifts panels on the wings that slow the plane down.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to lose speed or height.

controls.name: Flap lever

positions.text: Flaps are retracted for fast flight.
Flaps at 35 degrees, the most, for landing.

controls.text: This lever moves the flaps, parts of the wing which extend to give more lift at low speed.
controls.context: They are used for take-off and landing. The numbers are angles in degrees.

controls.name: Trim wheels / switches
controls.text: These controls trim the rudder and aileron. Trim is a small constant push so that the plane flies straight without pressure on the controls.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to remove a steady sideways pull.

controls.name: FMS CDUs (flight management keypads)
controls.text: Keypads with small screens. The pilot types the route and other flight data into the flight management system.
controls.context: The autopilot can then follow this route.

areas.name: Control wheel, throttles and pedals
areas.text: The controls the pilot holds or pushes with the feet.

panels.name: Control wheel, throttles and pedals
panels.text: The controls the pilot holds or pushes with the feet.
panels.context: The CJ4 is certified for a single pilot, so most things are within the pilot's reach.

controls.name: Control wheel
controls.text: Pushing the column forward points the nose down, pulling it back points it up. Turning the wheel rolls the plane left or right.
controls.context: The column moves the elevator on the tail and the wheel moves the ailerons on the wings.

controls.name: Pitch trim switch
controls.text: This thumb switch on the wheel horn trims the nose up or down.
controls.context: Trim takes away the steady force on the column.

controls.name: AP / trim disconnect
controls.text: This red button on the wheel switches the autopilot and the yaw damper off and interrupts the trim.
controls.context: It is how the pilot takes over the flying.

controls.name: Microphone switch
controls.text: While this switch on the wheel horn is pressed, the radio transmits.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to talk to air traffic control.

controls.name: Throttle 1
controls.text: This is the left throttle. It sets the power of the left engine, with notches for cutoff, idle, cruise, climb and take-off.
controls.context: The engine computer (FADEC) sets the power for each notch.

controls.name: Throttle 2
controls.text: This is the right throttle. It sets the power of the right engine.
controls.context: It is moved together with the left one in normal flight.

controls.name: TO/GA button
controls.text: This button on the outboard side of the left throttle selects the take-off mode of the flight director, or the go-around mode for a missed landing.
controls.context: The pilot presses it at the start of take-off or when breaking off an approach.

controls.name: Rudder pedals
controls.text: The pedals move the rudder on the tail to point the nose left or right. The tops of the pedals are the toe brakes for the left and right wheels.
controls.context: They also steer the nosewheel a few degrees.
